messages:
ken: hey, seeing intermittent packet loss between gpu-nodes during big training jobs. pods hit grpc EOFs and job step restarts. looks correlated with autoscale bursts (~40% CPU+net).

matt: any pings/traces yet? which pod/node pairs?

ken: reproduces on pool-gpu-eu-02 nodes (hostnames: eu-gpu-02-11/12). quick ping from node->node: ~0.4-1% loss, spikes when jobs saturate. matt asked for mtr, attaching short run:```
# mtr -r -c 20 eu-gpu-02-12
Start: 2026-03-16T14:02:01+0000
HOST: eu-gpu-02-11
1.|-- eu-gpu-02-12                                          0.0%  0.5ms
2.|-- 10.45.32.1 (geneve)                                   0.0%  0.7ms
3.|-- 10.45.32.2 (dst node)                                1.0% 13.2ms
```

jia: can you tcpdump the overlay? need to see re-transmits and encap packets.

ken: tcpdump attached (snippet). noticed lots of retransmits and some GENEVE packets with malformed inner frame?```
16:02:14.123456 IP4 eu-gpu-02-11 > eu-gpu-02-12: UDP, length 1424
16:02:14.123459 IP4 (encap:Geneve) 10.244.5.2 > 10.244.7.9: Flags [.], seq 12345:12589, ack 6789, win 65535
16:02:14.123460 IP4 eu-gpu-02-11 > eu-gpu-02-12: UDP, length 60  # ack lost later
```

olga: are NIC offloads on? any ethtool -k / -S outputs? mlx5 has known GSO/GRO quirks with geneve.

ken: ethtool -k shows gso/gro tcpv4 on, geneve checksums offload on. ethtool -S shows some "rx_no_buf" and "udp_gro" counters incrementing during bursts.```
# ethtool -k ens192
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
generic-segmentation-offload: on
receive-offload: on
generic-receive-offload: on
udp-fragmentation-offload: on

# ethtool -S ens192 | egrep "rx_no_buf|udp_gro"
rx_no_buf: 12
udp_gro: 48
```

matt: that matches an offload interaction hypothesis. when geneve/GRO tries to coalesce but inner frame sizes/metadata change, we can end up dropping or delivering out-of-order. did this start after the kernel bump a week ago?

ken: yes, kernel update landed in eu region on 2026-03-10, same timeframe as first reports.

jia: quick test suggestion: on one node, disable GRO+GSO for the overlay interface and run a short job. command:```
sudo ethtool -K geneve0 gro off gso off tso off
```

ken: doing that now on eu-gpu-02-11; will kick off a small 8-gpu training replica.

infra-bot: scheduled run: job/train-2026-03-16-ken-canary -> eu-gpu-02-11 -> STARTED

ken: after disabling, I see almost zero retransmits in tcpdump during the same load window. mtr shows 0.0% loss for the 2min run.

matt: OK promising. so likely kernel+offload regression. we should test: 1) revert kernel on a canary, 2) disable offloads cluster-wide as mitigation, 3) file bug with NIC vendor.

olga: also check for any recent changes to qdisc (fq_codel vs cake) or kube-proxy/iptables rules that might affect fragmentation.

ken: noted. I tested enabling fq_codel earlier — no clear delta.

jia: i'll open a tracking ticket and assign to net-team + infra for a rollback plan. can we add a temporary autoscale throttle for pool-gpu-eu-02 to reduce burstiness until we have a firm fix?

ken: yes please. reducing burst to 60% for the pool helps too (observed).

sre-oncall: copying oncall. if this affects customer workloads, we should notify CS with a short blurb.

matt: action items:```
- jia: create ticket + vendor bug
- ken: run offline kernel revert canary on eu-gpu-02-12
- olga: validate qdisc/iptables diff across versions
- infra: consider cluster-wide offload disable if rollback impossible
```

ken: will paste canary logs in ticket. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
